# Introduction

Introduce the background for your research and address three questions: Why
should readers care about this topic? What has already been done? What is new
in your proposed project?

Cite at least two relevant references in the introduction. Use the BibTeX keys
in `references.bib`. For example, cite a source in the text as
@agonafir2022machine, or cite it in parentheses as [@agonafir2022understanding].
Replace these example sources with work relevant to your project.

# Specific Aims

Formulate your research question or questions. Translate them into statistical
or data-science questions that you can address with the available data.

# Data

Identify the data needed for your project rather than stating that you will
try to find data. Describe the data source, coverage, key variables, and
structure, and explain why the data are suitable for your research questions.
Include relevant information about the observational unit, collection or
sampling process, time and geographic coverage, access, and use restrictions.

# Methods and Research Design

Describe the research design and methods you plan to use. Cite relevant
methodological references when appropriate. Explain how your planned modeling,
visualization, analysis, prediction, validation, or other methods will help
answer your research questions.

# Discussion

Identify the most challenging parts of the project and discuss its limitations.
Describe a fallback plan in case you encounter unexpected data, analytical, or
computational problems.
